mechanism_narrative: A four-week rise in WORKPLACES mobility from -26.3 to -16.4 signals restoration of commuting routines that increases weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -26.3 to -16.4 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to rise but the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the last-28-day mean, the commuting-recovery mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -45 removes travel friction and unlocks retail trips, so RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.3 to -42.0 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays above -45 for two consecutive weeks but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than last-28-day mean, the threshold claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous RESIDENTIAL decline from 9.6 to 5.9 and WORKPLACES rise from -26.3 to -16.4 indicates substitution from home to office and leisure, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 5.9 while WORKPLACES rose to -16.4
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL < 7.0 and WORKPLACES > -20.0 for two weeks but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not above last-28-day mean, the interaction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS printing negative for two consecutive weeks (-21.0 then -7.1) reflects cool/wet weather that shifts outdoor recreation demand to indoor retail, raising RETAIL_REC over one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS prints negative for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -21.0 in t-1w and -7.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS is negative for two consecutive weeks but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than last-28-day mean, the weather-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-lockdown policy reopening where TRANSIT is above -45, capacity limits on retail are relaxed, directly lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT > -45 and RETAIL_REC improves for two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -16.3 to -11.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If policy reopening is active and TRANSIT > -45 but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is below last-28-day mean, the relaxation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM staying below 5 for two consecutive weeks (3.4 then 2.7) shows no stockpiling, so household spending shifts to discretionary retail and lifts RETAIL_REC over one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean below 5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 3.4 in t-1w and 2.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM < 5 for two consecutive weeks but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not above last-28-day mean, the no-stockpiling mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals broad reopening that raises both weekday and weekend retail visits, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose to -16.4 and TRANSIT rose to -42.0
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than last-28-day mean, the joint-reopening mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL falling below 6.0 (5.9 in t-0w) signals a return to out-of-home routines, increasing retail trips and lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 to 5.9 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays below 6.0 but next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not above last-28-day mean, the out-of-home-routine mechanism fails.
